data.name: Lev
data.short_meaning: Aaron's son, attached to the tabernacle
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Lev means 'attached' or 'joined'. This name was given to the third son of Aaron, the high priest, and his descendants who served as priests in the tabernacle and later in the Temple. They were responsible for transporting the Ark of the Covenant and carrying the tabernacle and its implements. They were considered 'attached' to the Lord.

in_hebrew.name: לו
in_hebrew.meaning: לב means lion heart or courageous one in Hebrew
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם לו מקורו בשורש העברי לבב, שפירושו לב או courageous אחד. הוא קשור לנושאים של אומץ, חוזק, וסמליות האריה ביהדות. השם לו משמש לעיתים קרובות כקיצור לשמות שכוללים את השורש הזה, ומשדר אישיות חזקה ואמיצה.

in_greek.name: Λεβ
in_greek.meaning: Λεβ σημαίνει το λιοντάρι ή καρδιά λιονταριού
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Λεβ προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή ρίζα לבב, που σημαίνει καρδιά ή λιοντάρι. Στη Βιβλική παράδοση, το λιοντάρι είναι σύμβολο δύναμης και γενναιότητας. Το όνομα Λεβ χρησιμοποιείται ως σύμβολο της θαρραλέας και της θρησκευτικής πίστης.

data.cultural_impact: Lev was an important priestly family in ancient Israel, whose members, the Levites, were temple assistants and gatekeepers. They were responsible for different tasks, including singing in the Temple choir, maintaining the tabernacle and its implements, and carrying the Ark of the Covenant during the wilderness wanderings. Their role in the religious and cultural life of ancient Israel is still remembered and celebrated today. The name Lev thus carries a rich and enduring cultural significance as a symbol of priesthood and service to the Lord.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Bible, Lev is a name associated with service to God. It is the name of the third son of Aaron, the high priest, and his descendants who dedicated their lives to the service of God in the tabernacle and later in the Temple. The name Lev thus carries a deep spiritual significance as a reminder of the importance of devotion and service to God. It is a call to follow in the footsteps of the ancient Levites and to commit ourselves to God's service in whatever way we can.
